Another independent example: Panic by holding Pattern while on Song

Different starting point: Press Song (6,8). The Song page opens (Song Playback, SONG 01) and Song is the lit page button. Panic only works from the button of a page you are not on, so every other page button, including Pattern (5,8), is a panic button from here.

Open its full recorded scene: Panic by holding Pattern while on Song
03 / QUICK REFERENCE
Controls
Dense view
YOUR GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
Hold a non-selected page key (stopping first is optional)	Sweep Note Off across connected MIDI channels; holding the selected page key does not panic.
Evidence: release coverage
04 / MUSICAL EXAMPLES
Musical examples
RECIPE 01
Silence connected MIDI notes from Song view with the Channel panic gesture

Use this on a connected MIDI instrument when a note is stuck. The panic gesture sends note-release messages to connected MIDI outputs, but it does not stop the sequencer. The manual’s captured Output strip replays a recorded result; it does not send messages to your instrument.

Open Song at (6,8), so Channel is an inactive page button.
Hold Channel at (3,8) until the panic gesture fires, then release. The page remains Song.
A stuck MIDI note should stop; inspect the release messages in Output. The sequencer keeps running, so new notes may still play. Press Stop separately if you want silence to continue.

Use Silence a sounding note for the long-note comparison. The other examples show the gesture from a silent project.

RECIPE 02
Silence connected MIDI notes from Song view with the Pattern panic gesture

Use this on a connected MIDI instrument when a note is stuck. The panic gesture sends note-release messages to connected MIDI outputs, but it does not stop the sequencer. The manual’s captured Output strip replays a recorded result; it does not send messages to your instrument.

Open Song at (6,8), so Pattern is an inactive page button.
Hold Pattern at (5,8) until the panic gesture fires, then release. The page remains Song.
A stuck MIDI note should stop; inspect the release messages in Output. The sequencer keeps running, so new notes may still play. Press Stop separately if you want silence to continue.

Use Silence a sounding note for the long-note comparison. The other examples show the gesture from a silent project.
